card.title: M2A4
card.text: Has Blitz if it has 3 or more attack.
card.flavorText: The M2A4 was the ultimate version of the M2 light tank series, marking a crucial turning point in American armor development just prior to the US entry into WWII. It featured a single turret armed with a 37mm M5 gun and a total of five .30 caliber machine guns, positioned in the turret, bow, sponsons, and an anti-aircraft mount. With armor thickness increased to a maximum of 25mm, it was powered by a 250 hp radial engine, allowing for a top speed of 36 mph and a range of 200 miles. Built by the American Car & Foundry Company, 375 units were produced between 1940 and 1942. Unlike earlier American light tanks which carried only machine guns, the M2A4 reflected hard lessons learned from the Spanish Civil War, where tanks without cannons had proven useless against enemy armor. Although mostly used for training, the M2A4 saw significant combat with the US Marine Corps during the Guadalcanal campaign in 1942. Deployed by the 1st Tank Battalion, these tanks supported infantry assaults, neutralized Japanese bunkers, and used canister rounds effectively in defensive actions. Though soon superseded by the improved M3 Stuart, the M2A4 bridged the gap between interwar designs and the modern combat vehicles of WWII.
